sections.title: Objective type questions (2 parts of 1 mark, or 4 parts of ½ mark).

questions.q: Answer in one word each: (I) What is the system of flow of surface water mainly through rivers called? (II) What is the highest point or tip of a mountain range called?

or.q: Why does India have good trade relations with many countries across the sea?
or.answer: (1) India is surrounded by water from three sides. It commands sea routes between Europe and Africa, South- East Asia, far East Asia and Oceania. (2) It is because of this that India shares good trade relation between many countries since ancient times.

questions.q: Mention any two features of the Western Ghats.
questions.answer: (1) It runs parallel to the western coast for about 1600 km. Western ghats are continuous and can be crossed through passes like Pal Ghat, Thal Ghat and Bhor Ghat. (2) The highest peak in this region is Anaimudi (2695m.). They are good for generating hydropower because these rivers form rapids & water falls.

questions.q: Explain any two characteristics of the Northern Plains of India.
questions.answer: (1) This plain is one of the largest and most fertile plains of the world. This plain is formed due to deposits brought by the rivers like the Satluj, the Beas and the Ravi. The three main rivers in Himalayan system are the Indus, Ganga, The Brahmaputra. (2) From Punjab in the west to Assam in the east, this plain is about 2400 km long. Major crops such as wheat, rice, sugarcane, pulses, oil seeds and jute are grown here. Many cities are located along the rivers and are densely populated.

questions.q: Name two Purvanchal hills and mention the countries in which the Greater Himalaya is situated.
questions.answer: (1) Purvanchal hills: Patkai and Mizo (also Mishmi, Naga). (2) China, Bhutan, Tibet and Nepal lies to its north. It extends north of greater Himalaya and parallel to it is called zaskar range.

questions.q: What is a pass? Name any two passes situated in the Greater Himalaya.
questions.answer: (1) Pass: It is a natural gap or a route between a ridge, hill. Range: large landmass consisting of mountains, ridges and peaks. (2) High Mountain passes also exist in this range, namely, Bara Lacha-La, Shipki-La, Nathu-La, Zoji-La, Bomidi-La etc. It extends north of greater Himalaya and parallel to it is called zaskar range.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain any three differences between the Himalayan and the Peninsular drainage systems.
questions.answer: (1) They are Perennial rivers originating from glaciers. (2) These rivers have meandering courses which shift over time. (3) Most of the Peninsular rivers flow eastwards and enters into Bay of Bengal.

or.q: Explain any three main characteristics of the Western Ghats.
or.answer: (1) They run from west-east direction from Indus to Brahmaputra along the northern boundary of India 9.6), we will see the Western Ghats or Sahyadris lie on the Western edge of the Deccan plateau. It runs parallel to the western coast for about 1600 km. (2) They are continuous and higher than the Eastern Ghats (average 1,000 m); Anaimudi (2,695 m) is the highest peak, with Doda Betta and Makurti. (3) Western ghats are continuous and can be crossed through passes like Pal Ghat, Thal Ghat and Bhor Ghat. The rivers like Godavari, Bhima and Krishna flow eastward while the river Tapti flows westward. The streams form rapids & water falls before entering the Arabian Sea.

questions.q: 'India has a unique geographical location.' Support the statement.
questions.answer: (1) Teacher: India lies entirely in the northern hemisphere, and eastern hemisphere. The Tropic of Cancer (23°30′North) passes through the centre of the country. India is located between 8°4’ North and 37°6’ North lalitudes and 68°7’ East and 97°25’ longitudes. (2) It is surrounded by sea on three sides and lies at the centre of the Indian Ocean, commanding sea routes between Europe/Africa and East Asia, which helps trade. (3) The Himalayas form a natural barrier in the north, while passes link it with neighbours for trade and cultural exchange.

The Ganga and Yamuna rivers originates from this Himalayas. This is because most of these rivers originate from the glaciers and snowy (3) Everest, Kanchenjunga, Makalu, Dhaulagiri, Nanga Parbat etc. having a height of more than 8000 metres. High Mountain passes also exist in this range, namely, Bara Lacha-La, Shipki-La, Nathu-La, Zoji-La, Bomidi-La etc.

questions.q: What are the two divisions of the Northern Plains of India? Write two features of each.
questions.answer: (1) The Western Plain: formed by the Indus system rivers (Satluj, Beas, Ravi), lies west of the Aravallis, and has doabs — fertile land between two rivers. (2) The Ganga–Brahmaputra Plain: formed by the Ganga and Brahmaputra, very fertile and densely populated; early civilisations grew in such river valleys because of fertile land and water.

questions.q: Why are rivers important for life? Explain.
questions.answer: (1) Traditionally, rivers were useful as a source of abundant fresh water and navigation. In today’s world rivers importance has risen to include hydro power generation and setting up water-based industries. The rivers are ideal for irrigation purposes as they pass through plain fertile tracts. It is a table land made of old and metamorphosed rocks. (2) They carry fertile sediments, remove excess water and are used for navigation, hydro-power and tourism (boating, rafting). (3) Many cities are located along the rivers and are densely populated. questions.q: On the given outline map of India, mark and label: (A) Shimla, a tourist place in the Middle Himalaya (B) Western Ghats (C) River Krishna (D) Gir Range.
questions.answer: (A) Shimla — in Himachal Pradesh, about 31°N, 77°E, in the Lesser Himalaya (Himachal). (B) Western Ghats — a continuous line along the west coast from the Tapi (Maharashtra/Gujarat border) south to Kanyakumari. (C) Krishna — rises in the Western Ghats near Mahabaleshwar, flows east through Maharashtra, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh to the Bay of Bengal. (D) Gir Range — in the Kathiawar (Saurashtra) peninsula of Gujarat.

questions.q: On the given outline map of India, locate and label: (A) River Kaveri (B) Cardamom Hills (C) Chhota Nagpur Plateau (D) Nilgiri Hills.
questions.answer: (A) Kaveri — rises in the Western Ghats in Karnataka (Coorg), flows south-east through Karnataka and Tamil Nadu into the Bay of Bengal. (B) Cardamom Hills — southern Western Ghats on the Kerala–Tamil Nadu border. (C) Chhota Nagpur Plateau — Jharkhand and adjoining Chhattisgarh/West Bengal. (D) Nilgiri Hills — where the Western and Eastern Ghats meet, on the Tamil Nadu–Kerala–Karnataka border.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain India's geographical location with reference to its surrounding water bodies, neighbouring countries and southernmost points.
questions.answer: (1) The mainland extends from 8°4′N to 37°6′N and 68°7′E to 97°25′E; the Tropic of Cancer divides it into two halves and 82°30′E is the Standard Meridian. (2) Arabian sea in west, Bay of Bengal in the east and Indian ocean in the south. (3) Neighbours: Pakistan and Afghanistan (north-west); China, Nepal and Bhutan (north); Bangladesh and Myanmar (east); Sri Lanka across the Palk Strait and the Maldives (south). (4) The southern most point of the country is Indira Point (Nicobar Islands) which lies on 6°4′N latitudes and Kannya Kumari is southern most point of Indian mainland which lies on 8°4′ N latitudes. (5) India is strategically located in Indian Ocean. It commands sea routes between Europe and Africa, South- East Asia, far East Asia and Oceania. (i) The central Highlands: It extends from Narmada river and the northern plains. (6) The Himalayas protect it in the north while passes connect it with neighbours.

questions.q: Describe the six physical divisions of India.
questions.answer: (1) Northern Mountains — Himalayas (Himadri, Himachal, Shiwaliks), Trans-Himalaya (Karakoram, Ladakh, Zaskar) and Purvanchal hills. (2) From Punjab in the west to Assam in the east, this plain is about 2400 km long. This plain is one of the largest and most fertile plains of the world. Doab: the alluvial land between two converging rivers. The three main rivers in Himalayan system are the Indus, Ganga, The Brahmaputra. (3) River Narmada divides the peninsular plateau into two parts : The central highlands and Deccan Plateau The Nilgiri hills join Western & Eastern Ghats in the south. (4) Indian (Thar) Desert — west of the Aravallis, under 150 mm rain, sand dunes. (5) Coastal Plains — narrow western (Konkan, Karnataka, Malabar) and wider eastern (Northern Circars, Coromandel) with deltas. (6) There are 204 islands in Bay of Bengal called the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and 43 islands in Arabian Sea i.e Lakshadweep islands.
